records.text: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jedida daughter of Edeia, from Basouroth.
He did what was right in the Lord’s eyes and walked in every way of his father David, turning aside neither right nor left.
And the Lord God saw that the wickedness of mankind had multiplied upon the earth, and that each one continually set his heart upon evil all his days.
And God took to heart that He had made man upon the earth, and pondered it.
But Noah found grace before the Lord God.
Hear the Lord’s word, sons of Israel, for the Lord has a case against the land’s inhabitants: there is no truth, no mercy and no recognition of God upon the land.
Cursing, falsehood, murder, theft and adultery have poured over the land, and they mix bloodshed with bloodshed.
and say: Thus says the Lord: This is how I will smash this people and this city, as an earthenware vessel is smashed that cannot be healed again.
This is what I will do, says the Lord, to this place and its inhabitants, so that this city is made like the collapsing place.
Ephraim mingled among his peoples; Ephraim became a cake baked in ashes and not turned.
Foreigners devoured his strength, but he did not recognize it; gray hairs blossomed upon him, but he did not know it.
My sword became drunk in heaven. Behold, it will descend upon Idumea and upon the people of destruction, with judgment.
But if you have trusted false words from which you will receive no benefit,
Look, the wages of the laborers who reaped your fields, withheld by you, cry out; and the cries of the harvesters have entered the ears of the Lord Sabaoth.
The sinner provoked the Lord. According to the abundance of his anger, he will not seek out; God is not before him.
His ways are profaned at every time; Thy judgments are removed from before him; he will lord it over all his enemies.
For he said in his heart, “I will certainly not be shaken, from generation to generation, without adversity.”
His mouth is full of cursing, bitterness, and deceit; under his tongue are toil and trouble.
He sits in ambush with rich people, to kill an innocent person in hiding places; his eyes look toward the needy.
He lurks in hiding like a lion in its enclosure; he lurks to seize a poor man, to seize a poor man as he drags him away.
In his trap he will humble him; he will bow down and fall as he lords it over the needy.
Woe to those desiring the Lord’s day! Why is this Lord’s day for you? It is darkness, not light,
as when someone flees from a lion and a bear falls upon him, then leaps into his house, braces his hands upon the wall, and a snake bites him.
Is not the Lord’s day darkness rather than light, gloom that has no brightness in it?
They made choice ornaments a source of arrogance and made images of their abominations from them. Therefore I have given them over to them as uncleanness.
I will hand them into foreigners’ hands to plunder them, and to the pestilent people of the earth as spoils; they will profane them.
A righteous person, when he died, left regret, but the destruction of the impious is ready at hand and welcomed with joy.
Righteousness cuts blameless paths straight, but impiety falls into injustice.
The righteousness of upright men rescues them, but lawless people are caught in their own destruction.
“And now,” says the Lord your God, “turn to Me with your whole heart, with fasting, weeping and mourning.”
Tear your hearts, not your garments, and turn to the Lord your God, because He is merciful and compassionate, patient and abundant in mercy, and relents concerning calamities.
Who knows whether He will turn and relent and leave a blessing behind Him, a sacrifice and drink offering for the Lord our God?

There will no longer be a stronghold for Ephraim to flee to, nor a kingdom in Damascus, and the Syrians’ remainder will perish; for you are no better than Israel’s sons and their glory. Thus says the Lord Sabaoth.

Those in the Negeb will possess the mountain of Esau, and those in the Shephelah will possess the foreigners. They will possess the mountain of Ephraim, the plain of Samaria, Benjamin and the land of Gilead.

And this is the beginning of the deportation: for the sons of Israel, the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath; and the deportation of Jerusalem as far as Ephrathah. They will inherit the cities of the Negeb.
And men who have been saved shall ascend from Mount Zion to execute judgment upon the mountain of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the Lord’s.
And his wife looked behind her, and became a pillar of salt.
And Abraham rose early in the morning, and went to the place where he had stood before the Lord.
And he looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah, and toward the land of the surrounding country; and he saw, and behold, a flame rose from the earth as the vapour of a furnace.
And when the Lord blotted out all the cities of the surrounding country, God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out from the midst of the overthrow, when the Lord overthrew the cities where Lot lived.
“But you profane it by your saying, ‘The Lord’s table is polluted, and the foods placed upon it are despised.’
Your shepherds slumbered; the Assyrian king put your rulers to sleep. Your people departed upon the mountains, and there was no one receiving them.
There is no healing for your crushing; your wound has become inflamed. All who hear the report of you will clap their hands over you, for upon whom has your evil not continually come?

“Look, days are coming,” says the Lord, “when threshing will overtake the vintage and grapes will darken to ripeness at seedtime. The mountains will drip sweetness, and all the hills will be planted together.
I will plant them upon their land, and they will certainly never again be uprooted from the land I have given them,” says the Lord God Almighty.
For I have called upon the name of the Lord; ascribe greatness unto our God.
“For look, in those days and at that time, when I turn back the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem,
and cast lots over My people; they gave the boys to prostitutes and sold the girls for wine, which they drank.
And at Burning, and at Testing, and at the Graves of Desire, you provoked the Lord your God.
For all the peoples will walk, each his own way, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and beyond.

He will destroy chariots from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem; the battle bow will be destroyed, and abundance and peace from the nations. He will rule waters as far as the sea and the earth’s river outlets.
“Oh! Oh! Flee from the northern land,” says the Lord, “because I will gather you from the four winds of heaven,” says the Lord.
Escape safely to Zion, you who dwell in daughter Babylon!
For thus says the Lord Almighty: “After glory He has sent me against the nations that plundered you, for whoever touches you is like one touching the pupil of his eye.
Look, I am bringing My hand against them, and they will become spoils for those serving them; you will know that the Lord Almighty has sent me.”
Many nations will take refuge with the Lord on that day and become His people. They will dwell within you, and you will recognize that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you.
The Lord will inherit Judah as His portion on the holy land and again choose Jerusalem.
Let all flesh be reverent before the Lord, for He has risen from His holy clouds.
You will no longer be called Abandoned, nor will your land be called Desert. You will be called My Desire, and your land Inhabited.
then the Lord shall heal your sins, and have mercy upon you, and shall gather you again from all the nations whither the Lord has scattered you.
If your dispersion is from one end of heaven unto the other end of heaven, from thence shall the Lord your God gather you, and from thence shall the Lord your God take you.
And the Lord your God shall bring you into the land which your fathers inherited, and you shall inherit it; and He shall do you good, and make you more numerous than your fathers.
